Está pensado para ordenadores con teclado; el juego está en español y la partida no se guarda al cerrar o recargar la página. La edición CPC de 64K se ejecuta mediante la emulación compatible de CPC 6128 en RVMPlayer.
-
Recorrer la abadía. Las 93 estancias aparecen en su lugar real: explora plantas, luz y versiones. ![Atlas de las estancias de la abadía](assets/readme/preview-room-atlas-cropped.png) El atlas sitúa 93 estancias en su posición real: 61 en la planta principal, 16 en el scriptorium y 16 en la biblioteca. Puedes abrir cualquiera a tamaño completo, desplazarte espacialmente a las contiguas con teclado, controles en pantalla o gestos, alternar día y noche y comparar CPC, ZX Spectrum, MSX, PC CGA, PCW y el remake PC VGA. El mapa ampliado de *Extensum* añade 140 estancias cartografiadas, distribuidas por plantas y explorables de día y de noche.
-
Ver nacer una estancia. Sigue sus 32 colocaciones y el viaje de cada píxel hasta la pantalla. ![Reconstrucción paso a paso de una estancia](assets/readme/preview-room-construction-cropped.png) La demostración interactiva de la estancia 17 reproduce sus 32 colocaciones una a una, aísla la receta arquitectónica activa y explica qué teselas gráficas (tiles) y celdas modifica. Una segunda fase sigue la copia documentada de las 320 celdas visibles a la pantalla CGA. Todo puede avanzarse manualmente o reproducirse, de día y de noche.
-
Leer los pergaminos. Cada letra aparece trazo a trazo, con sus pausas y su música. ![Manuscrito reconstruido trazo a trazo](assets/readme/preview-manuscript-cropped.png) No son textos que simplemente aparecen: cada letra se traza píxel a píxel, con sus pausas y pasos de página. Los controles permiten reproducir, pausar, completar la página, reiniciar y cambiar la velocidad. La versión gráfica seleccionada transforma el manuscrito y activa su música correspondiente en CPC, ZX Spectrum, MSX, PC CGA, PCW o remake VGA.
-
Seguir los siete días. 41 momentos documentados, personajes en movimiento y secretos protegidos por spoilers. ![Explorador de los siete días](assets/readme/preview-seven-days-cropped.png) El explorador recorre 41 momentos desde nona del día I hasta tercia del VII. Primero ofrece una crónica sin spoilers; después permite abrir las pistas, los sucesos, qué hacer y los diálogos correspondientes. El mapa sitúa a los ocho personajes y muestra sus desplazamientos esperados entre horas o dentro de escenas documentadas, con retratos seleccionables, orígenes, destinos y estados de presencia. Es una lectura editorial de la lógica reconstruida del juego —no un emulador ni una repetición de una partida— y señala cuándo los encuentros pueden variar por cercanía, inventario o acciones anteriores.
-
Escuchar la abadía. Ave María, la acusación «pirata», pasos, efectos y la huella sonora de cada máquina. ![Archivo sonoro de La Abadía](assets/readme/preview-ave-maria-cropped.png) El archivo sonoro permite reproducir la muestra digital original de *Ave María* del PC, la acusación «pirata», melodías reconstruidas desde el ejecutable DOS, pasos y efectos, además de recreaciones del sonido del Amstrad CPC y del PCW.
-
Entender el motor. Del mundo de coordenadas a la piedra isométrica: teselas, máscaras, capas y luz. ![Atlas de teselas gráficas del motor](assets/readme/preview-graphics-tiles.png) Las descripciones recuperadas de 116 estancias, 2.497 colocaciones arquitectónicas, 87 recetas y 256 teselas explican cómo una posición del mundo termina convertida en una pantalla isométrica. El recorrido continúa por máscaras, capas de profundidad, paletas, iluminación, objetos, puertas, rutas, estados de los personajes y trucos de cámara.
-
Investigar el legado. Versiones, fuentes, prensa, remakes y Extensum, reunidos en un archivo vivo. ![Seis revistas y páginas históricas](assets/readme/preview-magazines-cropped.png) Ocho personajes con agendas propias, objetos y llaves, Obsequium, mapas, laberinto, cronología, adaptaciones, publicidad, prensa española y británica, reconstrucciones técnicas y el legado de una obra irrepetible.
### Seis rutas, incluida una guía técnica | Ruta | Qué encontrarás | | --- | --- | | [Historia](es/index.html) | Paco Menéndez, Juan Delcán, el origen del proyecto, las adaptaciones y su compleja historia editorial. | | [El juego](es/juego.html) | Pergaminos interactivos, personajes, objetos, siete jornadas con cronología hora a hora, mapas y el atlas completo de estancias. | | [Programación](es/tecnica.html) | Versiones, sonido, *Ave María*, protección anticopia, inteligencia de los personajes y acceso a la guía gráfica completa. | | [Guía del motor gráfico](es/graficos.html) | De coordenadas, descripciones y recetas a teselas, capas, máscaras y la construcción interactiva de una estancia. | | [Prensa y anuncios](es/prensa.html) | Publicidad y páginas históricas españolas y británicas, examinables con el visor y sus controles de zoom. | | [Legado](es/legado.html) | Recuperaciones, remakes, influencia, preservación y memoria del juego. | La cabecera mantiene la versión gráfica elegida mientras cambias de ruta. Pantallas, personajes, objetos, indicador de Obsequium, atlas, materiales técnicos y pergaminos responden a esa selección. La edición española y la inglesa son recorridos completos e independientes. ## English This tribute does more than tell the story of *La Abadía del Crimen*: it lets you walk through it, listen to it, and take it apart piece by piece. The game, its creators and ports, the abbey’s architecture, character routines, the seven-day investigation, sound, contemporary press, code archaeology, and its legacy all meet in an editorial experience designed for exploration. ### What you can do (open each section to learn more) -
Play in your browser. Ten preserved editions, loaded directly in your browser. ![Browser player for the preserved editions](assets/readme/preview-player.png)
  • Amstrad CPC 6128 · full abbey (128K)

Each disk or tape loads automatically, and the player provides pause, mute, restart, and full screen. It is designed for computers with a keyboard; the game is in Spanish, and progress is not saved when you close or reload the page. The 64K CPC edition runs through the compatible CPC 6128 emulation in RVMPlayer.
-
Walk the abbey. All 93 rooms in their real positions—explore floors, light, and versions. ![Atlas of the abbey rooms](assets/readme/preview-room-atlas-cropped.png) The atlas places 93 rooms in their real positions: 61 on the main floor, 16 in the scriptorium, and 16 in the library. Open any room at full size, move spatially to its neighbours with the keyboard, on-screen controls, or gestures, switch between day and night, and compare CPC, ZX Spectrum, MSX, PC CGA, PCW, and the PC VGA remake. The expanded *Extensum* map adds 140 mapped rooms across its floors, explorable by day and night.
-
Watch a room take shape. Follow its 32 placements and every pixel’s journey to the screen. ![Step-by-step room reconstruction](assets/readme/preview-room-construction-cropped.png) The interactive room-17 demonstration replays all 32 placements, isolates the active architectural recipe, and explains which tiles and cells it changes. A second phase follows the documented transfer of all 320 visible cells to the CGA screen. Step through it manually or press play, by day or by night.
-
Read the manuscripts. Every letter appears stroke by stroke, with its pauses and music. ![Manuscript reconstructed stroke by stroke](assets/readme/preview-manuscript-cropped.png) These are not blocks of text that simply appear: every letter is drawn pixel by pixel, with the original pauses and page turns. Play, pause, complete a page, restart, or change speed. The selected graphical version transforms the manuscript and supplies its matching CPC, ZX Spectrum, MSX, PC CGA, PCW, or VGA remake music.
-
Follow seven days. 41 documented moments, moving characters, and spoiler-gated secrets. ![Seven-day explorer](assets/readme/preview-seven-days-cropped.png) The explorer covers 41 moments from none on day I to terce on day VII. It begins with a spoiler-free chronicle, then lets you open the clues, events, suggested actions, and relevant dialogue. The map places all eight characters and shows their expected movements between hours or across documented scenes, with selectable portraits, origins, destinations, and presence states. This is an editorial reading of the reconstructed game logic—not an emulator or recorded playthrough—and it identifies encounters that may change with proximity, inventory, or earlier actions.
-
Hear the abbey. The journey continues through masks, depth layers, palettes, lighting, objects, doors, routes, character states, and camera tricks.
-

# Status Journal

Newest entry first. Each entry: date, what was done, what was learned, what is next.
Subsystem details live in `progress/*.md`; this file is the project journal.

## 2026-10-08 — Session 3 (night): smooth flight (R2b)

### Done
- ADR-019: the space view moves at the display rate. Sprites carry their state of the tick before
  (`SpriteInstance.HasPrevious`/`Previous*`, `At(t)`), paired by slot, occurrence and
  `SpawnId` (new port field of `SpaceObject`, set whenever a slot gets a new object); engine
  flames and turrets follow their parent's sprite; target brackets (stretched one-pixel sprites)
  and the lock spiral are sprites tied to the target. `SpaceView.PresentedAt`/`TickMilliseconds`,
  `GameRuntime` sets `RenderFrame.Interpolation` after every update; the Vulkan sprite pass and the
  CPU reference draw `At(Interpolation)` (with a separate vertical scale).
- wc1tool `snap --interpolate`: renders what the window shows at the given time (checked: bolts,
  ships, flames and brackets halfway between two ticks).
- Noticed while testing (unchanged, as in the Kilrathi Saga code): the guns fire on key-repeat events, so
  pressing a turn key while Space is held stops the auto-repeat and the guns (turn first, then
  fire, works).
- Tests: Core 65, Graphics 180, Audio 240, Simulation 418, Render.Vulkan 106, Game 272,

simonalling-zatacka-decomp-build-py.text:
"""Builds zatacka.cpp with Borland C++ 3.1 in headless DOSBox: the result is byte-identical to ZATACKA.EXE.

Usage:  [ALLOW_MISMATCH=1] [INCLUDE_MAP_AND_ASM=1] python build.py OUTDIR
  ALLOW_MISMATCH=1        exit successfully even if output does not match original ZATACKA.EXE (useful for deliberate modifications)
  INCLUDE_MAP_AND_ASM=1   also output ZATACKA.MAP (linker map) and ZATACKA.ASM (BCC -S listing)
  OUTDIR                  emptied, then gets ZATACKA.EXE + EGAVGA.BGI/TSCR.CHR to run it
Needs: dosbox (0.74).  The floppy images are FAT12; the installer's ZIPs use PKZIP 1.x
"implode", so they are unpacked with the UNZIP.EXE from disk 1 inside DOSBox.  BCC needs TASM for the inline asm.
"""

import os
import shutil
import struct
import subprocess
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
# Small model, speed optimizations, inline functions out of line (random() is a call), compile via TASM (-B): the
# original went through single-pass TASM, which leaves "jg $+5 / jmp short / nop" for one forward branch in main.
OPTIONS = os.environ.get("BCC_OPTIONS", "-ms -O2 -vi- -B")
FIXED_MTIME = 700000000  # 1992-03-07
OUTPUTS = ["ZATACKA.EXE", "ZATACKA.MAP", "ZATACKA.ASM", "EGAVGA.BGI", "TSCR.CHR"]
# Unpacked BC++ installation (C: in DOSBox), reused across builds:
CACHE = os.path.join(HERE, ".cache")
DOSROOT = os.path.join(CACHE, "dosroot")
# the BC++ 3.1 installation floppies needed, from the 3.5" 1.44 MB set
DISKS = [
    "Disk01.img",
    "Disk02.img",
    "Disk03.img",
    "Disk07.img",
    "Disk08.img",
    "Disk09.img",
    "Disk13.img",
]
# zip (or split .CA* parts, concatenated) -> install directory
PARTS = [
    (["CMDLINE.CA1", "CMDLINE.CA2"], "BIN"),
    (["BIN.ZIP"], "BIN"),
    (["TASM.CA1", "TASM.CA2"], "BIN"),
    (["INCLUDE.ZIP"], "INCLUDE"),
    (["SLIB.ZIP"], "LIB"),
    (["XLIB.ZIP"], "LIB"),
    (["BGI.ZIP"], "BGI"),
]


def fat12_files(img):
    """{NAME.EXT: bytes} of the root directory of a FAT12 floppy image (the BC++ disks have no subdirectories)."""
    d = open(img, "rb").read()
    bps, spc, rsv, nfat, nroot, _, _, spf = struct.unpack_from("<HBHBHHBH", d, 11)
    fat = d[rsv * bps : (rsv + spf) * bps]
    root = (rsv + nfat * spf) * bps
    data = root + nroot * 32
    csize = spc * bps
    out = {}
    for i in range(root, data, 32):
        e = d[i : i + 32]
        if e[0] == 0:
            break
        if e[0] == 0xE5 or e[11] & 0x18:
            continue
        name = e[0:8].decode("cp437").rstrip() + "." + e[8:11].decode("cp437").rstrip()
        c, size, buf = (
            struct.unpack_from("<H", e, 26)[0],
            struct.unpack_from("<I", e, 28)[0],
            b"",
        )
        while 2 <= c < 0xFF8 and len(buf) < size:
            buf += d[data + (c - 2) * csize : data + (c - 1) * csize]
            v = struct.unpack_from("<H", fat, c * 3 // 2)[0]
            c = v >> 4 if c & 1 else v & 0xFFF
        out[name.rstrip(".")] = buf[:size]
    return out


def dosbox(root, batch):
    """Run C:\\RUN.BAT (with root as C:) in headless DOSBox; returns C:\\OUT.TXT."""
    open(os.path.join(root, "RUN.BAT"), "w", newline="\r\n").write(batch)
    conf = os.path.join(root, "dosbox.conf")
    open(conf, "w").write(
        "[sdl]\noutput=surface\n[dosbox]\nmemsize=16\n[cpu]\ncore=dynamic\ncycles=max\n[mixer]\nnosound=true\n"
        f'[autoexec]\nmount c "{root}"\nc:\ncall RUN.BAT\nexit\n'
    )
    env = dict(os.environ, SDL_VIDEODRIVER="dummy", SDL_AUDIODRIVER="dummy")
    subprocess.run(
        ["dosbox", "-conf", conf, "-noconsole"],
        env=env,
        capture_output=True,
        timeout=600,
    )
    p = os.path.join(root, "OUT.TXT")
    return (
        open(p, encoding="cp437").read().replace("\r", "") if os.path.exists(p) else ""
    )


def install(root):
    files = {}
    for disk in DISKS:
        files.update(fat12_files(os.path.join(HERE, "borland", disk)))
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(root, "ZIPS"))
    open(os.path.join(root, "UNZIP.EXE"), "wb").write(files["UNZIP.EXE"])
    lines = [f"mkdir BC\\{d}" for d in ("BIN", "INCLUDE", "LIB", "BGI")]
    lines[:0] = ["mkdir BC"]
    for i, (parts, dst) in enumerate(PARTS):
        open(os.path.join(root, "ZIPS", f"P{i}.ZIP"), "wb").write(
            b"".join(files[p] for p in parts)
        )
        lines.append(f"UNZIP ZIPS\\P{i}.ZIP BC\\{dst} >> C:\\OUT.TXT")
    log = dosbox(root, "\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(root, "BC", "BIN", "BCC.EXE")):
        sys.exit("unpacking failed:\n" + log)


def main():
    allow_mismatch = os.environ.get("ALLOW_MISMATCH") == "1"
    include_map_and_asm = os.environ.get("INCLUDE_MAP_AND_ASM") == "1"
    outdir = sys.argv[1]
    # Empty OUTDIR, but only if it holds nothing but earlier build output (so a wrong path can't wipe anything else):
    if os.path.exists(outdir):
        unexpected = sorted(set(os.listdir(outdir)) - set(OUTPUTS))
        if unexpected:
            sys.exit(f"{outdir} contains files not produced by the build, so it won't be emptied: {unexpected}")
        shutil.rmtree(outdir)
    os.makedirs(outdir)
    if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(DOSROOT, "BC", "BIN", "BCC.EXE")):
        shutil.rmtree(DOSROOT, ignore_errors=True)
        os.makedirs(CACHE, exist_ok=True)
        open(os.path.join(CACHE, ".gitignore"), "w").write("*\n")
        install(DOSROOT)
    w = os.path.join(DOSROOT, "W")
    shutil.rmtree(w, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(w)
    shutil.copy(
        os.path.join(HERE, "zatacka.cpp"), os.path.join(w, "ZATACKA.CPP")
    )
    for d, _, ns in os.walk(
        DOSROOT
    ):  # fixed file dates: BCC -S records them in ?debug lines
        for n in ns:
            os.utime(os.path.join(d, n), (FIXED_MTIME, FIXED_MTIME))
    batch = (
        "set PATH=C:\\BC\\BIN\ncd W\n"
        f"BCC {OPTIONS} -lm -IC:\\BC\\INCLUDE -LC:\\BC\\LIB ZATACKA.CPP GRAPHICS.LIB > C:\\OUT.TXT\n"
    )
    if include_map_and_asm:
        batch += f"BCC {OPTIONS.replace('-B', '')} -S -IC:\\BC\\INCLUDE ZATACKA.CPP >> C:\\OUT.TXT\n"
    log = dosbox(DOSROOT, batch)
    print(log.strip(), flush=True)
    if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(w, "ZATACKA.EXE")):
        sys.exit("build failed")
    shutil.copy(os.path.join(w, "ZATACKA.EXE"), outdir)
    if include_map_and_asm:
        for f in ("ZATACKA.MAP", "ZATACKA.ASM"):
            if os.path.exists(os.path.join(w, f)):
                shutil.copy(os.path.join(w, f), outdir)
    for f in ("EGAVGA.BGI", "TSCR.CHR"):  # loaded at runtime from the current directory
        shutil.copy(os.path.join(DOSROOT, "BC", "BGI", f), outdir)
    same = {}
    for f in ("ZATACKA.EXE", "EGAVGA.BGI", "TSCR.CHR"):
        same[f] = (
            open(os.path.join(outdir, f), "rb").read()
            == open(os.path.join(HERE, "original-game", f), "rb").read()
        )
        print(
            f"{f} is byte-identical to the original"
            if same[f]
            else f"{f} differs from the original"
        )
    ok = allow_mismatch or (
        same["ZATACKA.EXE"]
        and same["EGAVGA.BGI"]
        and same["TSCR.CHR"]
    )
    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Runtime and acceptance status

The preservation executable links and starts through original `Setup_Game`.
Connected automated coverage reaches original-asset startup, title flow, new
game setup, Citadel exploration, menus, services, training, Mech combat,
save/load and normal shutdown.

The latest recorded local baseline is:

- 113 passing asset-independent headless tests;
- 164 passing SDL/original-asset tests; and
- successful Debug and Release linkage of the game executable.

The SDL count includes opt-in tests using the owner's private installation;
the headless count is the public, asset-independent repository baseline.

## Known limits

- No complete manual playthrough has been certified.
- Video composition and PC-speaker/music output have connected tests but are
  not pixel-, cycle- or waveform-identical certifications.
- Several exceptional native paths depend on stack or residual storage that
  portable C cannot reproduce safely without more calling-context evidence.
- Original assets are required for normal play and are not distributed.

The detailed historic boundary list and acceptance checklist are retained in
[`history/PLAYABLE_BUILD_2026-09-18.md`](history/PLAYABLE_BUILD_2026-09-18.md).
Treat its old paths and build commands as a dated record.

# Campaign acceptance record

This document separates the repeatable automated smoke path from broader manual
play testing. Neither is a claim that the complete campaign is verified.

## Automated smoke path

Established on 2026-09-29, the smoke path runs the SDL executable against a
private original-game installation. `REVENGE_SMOKE_INPUT` supplies delayed raw
keyboard values at the SDL input boundary; it does not bypass menus or call
game procedures directly.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Title resources render before input | Pass |
| Main-menu keyboard navigation | Pass |
| New Game dispatches campaign stage 0 | Pass |
| Original save container can be loaded | Pass |
| Loaded campaign stage dispatches | Pass |
| Tactical resources, units and first frame initialize | Pass |
| Tactical interaction loop is entered | Pass |
| Confirmed title/options shutdown returns zero | Pass |

The original raw keys used by this harness include Enter `002B`, Escape
`006E`, Right `0066`, Down `0062` and Up `0060`. The harness is optional and is
inactive unless `REVENGE_SMOKE_INPUT` is set.

## Manual acceptance

Manual play testing has completed campaign missions 1 through 6. This covers
substantially more than the scripted tactical-entry smoke test, including
campaign transitions, lance assignment, tactical movement and targeting,
combat, mission completion, debriefing and continued save/campaign state.

The last behavior-changing acceptance baseline is commit `59f8cdab`. Later
commits through the documentation cleanup are preservation accounting,
repository organization and annotation readability work.

## Remaining validation

- Complete the remaining campaign and alternate branches.
- Exercise more save/load points across campaign stages.
- Compare presentation timing and audio effects with an original DOS run.
- Retest uncommon adapters and configuration combinations where practical.
- Record any discovered defect with the campaign stage, save state, input mode
  and trace output needed to reproduce it.

Original saves and assets used for acceptance remain private and are not part
of the repository.

missingno7-m602-scr-docs-fidelity-md.text:
# Fidelity

Reference: the [m602_recon](https://github.com/missingno7/m602_recon) matching
decompilation, `src/SAVER.PAS`, which is relocation-equivalent to overlay 61 of
`M602X.EXE`, and its notes `docs/notes/saver.md` and `saver_handoff.md`.
Addresses are in its `res:SEG:OFS` / `ovl:N:OFS` notation.

## Translated from the original (`src/saver.cpp`)

| Original | Notes |
|---|---|
| `ScreenSaver` `ovl:61:06D8` | same statements and order; `Integer` = `int16_t`, `Word` = `uint16_t`, `Boolean` = byte |
| `Draw` `ovl:61:0121` | erase the trailing column/row of every box, then draw boxes 1, 2, 3; date and time re-read every frame |
| `DrawString` `ovl:61:0000` | `Byte` X/Y, 16-bit offset `(Y*ScreenWidth+X)*2`, `lodsb/stosw/loop` |
| `Pause` `ovl:61:0073` | `(Ticks-FirstTick)*55` in LongInt, both tick reads, midnight exit |
| TP 6.01 `Random`, `Randomize` | `RandSeed*134775813+1`, `(RandSeed shr 16) mod n`, seed from INT 21h AH=2Ch |
| `res:119C:0201`, `Maximum`/`Minimum`, `Drivers.ClearScreen` | digit formatting, signed LongInt clamps, fill with `0720h` |
| `DS:539C`, `DS:53D8`, `DS:53DE` | box lines, initial directions |

The screen is an emulated 32 KB B800h text buffer of character/attribute
words. The saver writes it as the original did and never clears it between
frames; the renderer only reads it.

## Replaced machine dependencies

| Original | Replacement |
|---|---|
| BIOS tick count `0:046C` (18.2065 Hz, wraps at 1800B0h) | computed from the monotonic clock, phase from the time of day (`src/biostime.h`; `winmachine.h`, `posixmachine.h`) |
| INT 28h in Pause's busy-wait | sleep until the next tick; Pause's exit depends only on the tick count, so frames happen at the same ticks without using the CPU |
| other INT 28h calls | omitted (no observable effect) |
| DOS GetDate / GetTime | local time |
| `Application^.GetEvent` | input events from the window on Windows; on macOS the system ends the saver |
| VGA scan-out | `src/renderer.cpp` |
| cursor parking, mouse hiding | no text cursor drawn; mouse pointer hidden |

## Adaptations

- **Text width.** `ScreenWidth` is `round(60 × width/height)` (80 on 4:3, 96 on
  16:10, 107 on 16:9, 140 on 21:9), clamped to 41..255. The original movement
  rules handle any width via `MaxX = ScreenWidth - 11`. Rows, box size, start
  column 30 and speed are unchanged. The text area is fitted with the original
  proportions, which can leave margins of a few pixels. The *80×25* setting
  keeps 80 columns.
- **Uninitialized locals.** `StepY` and `Cycle` are never set in the original;
  their values are leftover stack contents. The port starts with `False` and
  `1`, so all boxes keep their initial directions until box 1's first periodic
  re-roll at frame 5.
- **Exit.** Key press, mouse button or wheel, or moving the mouse more than
  4 px ends the saver at its next event check. Turbo Vision also ignored
  movement within one text cell.
- **Not ported:** idle activation, mouse-corner and modem triggers, and saving
  and restoring the underlying screen.
- **Multiple monitors:** each monitor runs its own saver, sized to its shape.
- **Speed setting:** the emulated tick rate is scaled. Pause still waits
  2 ticks and the sequence of frames is identical.
- **Color setting:** replaces palette entry 7 (`#AAAAAA`), the only colour
  the saver uses.

## Display

- 9×16 cells with the VGA line-graphics rule: the 9th column repeats the 8th
  for C0h–DFh, so box lines join.
- 720×400 is shown as 4:3, so raster pixels are 20:27, not square.
- Area-weighted resampling in linear light keeps raster pixels equal in size
  at fractional scales.
- Optional scanlines follow the 400 logical raster lines.
- Font: M602 loads its own KeybCS set by default (help text: "Nezavádět font"
  turns this off). Its `f` and `7` differ from the IBM ROM font. The block at
  file offset BEF9Fh of `M602X.EXE` was identified by content: KeybCS layout,
  87h = č, 9Fh = ť.

## Verification (`tests/`)

- **DOS reference:** `gen_reference.py` compiles the unmodified `SAVER.PAS`
  with Turbo Pascal 6.01 and runs it under MS-DOS Player with:
  - a scripted DOS clock;
  - INT 28h advancing the tick count;
  - `StepY`/`Cycle` preset in their stack slots.

  It logs the seed, positions, directions, `Cycle`, `StepY` and a screen hash
  after every frame. The C++ port matches all 6,300 frames: widths 80, 107,
  140 and 41, and initial `(StepY, Cycle)` of `(F,1)`, `(T,0)` and `(T,3)`.
- **Screen:** after every frame the screen equals a blank screen with boxes
  1, 2, 3 drawn in order, so no stale cells are left behind.
- **PRNG:** a register-level transcription of `res:1570:1726` matches the
  port.
- **Timing:**
  - With a simulated clock, frames come exactly 2 ticks apart, and the wait
    is 1 tick across midnight.
  - In real time, frames measured 109.86 ms apart (expected 109.85 ms) with
    about 0 % CPU.

## Open points

- The initial `StepY`/`Cycle` values (see Adaptations).
- Palette shades and screen mode can be changed in M602; the defaults are
  assumed.
- The code path that loads the font block was not traced.
- Not modelled: the original read the tick count in two word reads, which can
  tear once an hour, and a frame being scanned out while half drawn.

decisions.title: SimonAlling/kurve
decisions.reason: Elm/browser remake is not established as source-derived by inspected README. Followed its explicit original-source link and promoted the separate zatacka-decomp matching project instead.

decisions.title: andresdelcampo/HomenajeLaAbadiaDelCrimen
decisions.reason: Useful visual/editorial research companion with decoded assets and room demonstrations, but playable original editions use emulators. Keep as a companion lead, not a new native game reconstruction; narrative seven-day paths explicitly are not a replay or full engine simulation.
